_comment: ClinePass pricing (USD per 1M tokens), transcribed from the Reference pricing table on docs.cline.bot/getting-started/clinepass. Regenerated 2026-09-21. A runtime refresher rewrites this hourly; this baseline is what a failed refresh falls back to.

This is the platform's own published table and the only complete one it offers: ClinePass is a flat $9.99/month subscription, so these rates are not what the user is charged - they are the reference rates ClinePass measures quota consumption against. That makes them the right basis for this proxy's cost column, which estimates consumption rather than billing.

Do NOT source this table from models.dev. Its cline-pass provider exists (15 models) and agrees row-for-row on 11 of these 13, but its deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-pro rows are byte-identical to its own mimo-v2.5 and mimo-v2.5-pro rows - a mapping error, not a peak rate. Taking those two from models.dev would under-price real traffic by ~2x.

SOURCE SPLIT - 13 of the 15 rules below are transcribed verbatim from the Reference pricing table (the 'Published rows'). The remaining two, glm-5.3-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash, are NOT on that page: they appear in the live recommended-models roster and are priced here from models.dev, which is a third party. They are marked individually. Re-check them first when the docs page is next revised.

cline-pass/muse-spark-1.3-contributor also appears in the live roster and has no rule here on purpose: neither source publishes a rate for it, so its cost reports as unknown. A missing rule is not a zero rate - inventing one would show a confident, wrong number.

Rows carry the platform's own model id (the page's Model ID table gives it as cline-pass/<name>), matched as a substring with longest-match winning. The full id is used rather than the bare name so a rule cannot match a same-named model on another platform and so the seed reads identically to what the live refresher parses off the page. glm-5.3 is a substring of glm-5.3-flash and mimo-v2.5 of mimo-v2.5-pro, which is why the longer id must stay in this table - longest match decides, not row order. Base rates are the Off-peak column; `tiers` replace them once the whole prompt exceeds `size` input tokens, matching the table's own '> 256K tokens' wording.

DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash publish a Peak column too (1.32/3.96/0.044 and 0.44/1.32/0.014). An earlier revision of this note said the peak WINDOW was unverified; it is verifiable, from the page this table's own footnote cites. DeepSeek's pricing page states: "Peak hours are 01:00 - 04:00 and 06:00 - 10:00 UTC, Monday through Friday, excluding Chinese public holidays". peakSchedules therefore carries a cline-pass entry with excludesHolidays set, and these rows bill at Peak inside that window on a working day.
